text:
Baywater Gazette reporter on the quayside at the Calder Basin Oceanographic Institute watched the Marisol Trench probe reach its maximum depth of 6,100 metres on 14 March 2031, and saw the final sounding come through on the control-room screens.

Dr. Ilvane Torsk, the institute's chief scientist, led the mission. She told me the descent took 4 hours 52 minutes. The probe's pressure sensors logged 610 bar at the lowest point.

Staff in the room stood as the last data packet arrived. Dr. Torsk confirmed the transmission was complete before anyone left their seat.

The institute released Mission Summary Report CB-31-07 the day after the dive. It sets out the depth, the descent time and the pressure reading in the same figures Dr. Torsk gave me at the control desk.

The probe reached 6,100 metres.
